#include <stdio.h>

// ── Function prototypes (declarations before main) ────────────
// Tells compiler the function exists before we define it
int    add(int a, int b);             // returns int, takes two ints
double power(double base, int exp);   // returns double
void   printTable(int n, int upto);   // returns nothing (void)
void   swap(int *a, int *b);          // pointers allow modifying caller's variables

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    printf("add(3,4) = %d\n", add(3, 4));        // 7
    printf("2^10 = %.0f\n", power(2, 10));        // 1024.0 (%.0f = no decimals)
    printTable(5, 5);                              // multiplication table of 5

    int x = 10, y = 20;                                // integer variable
    printf("Before swap: x=%d y=%d\n", x, y);          // output print karo
    swap(&x, &y);                                  // pass addresses so function can modify them
    printf("After  swap: x=%d y=%d\n", x, y);    // x=20 y=10

    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}

// ── Function definitions ───────────────────────────────────────
int add(int a, int b) {                                // integer return karne wala function
    return a + b;           // return sum back to caller
}

double power(double base, int exp) {   // recursive power function
    if (exp == 0) return 1;            // base case: anything^0 = 1
    return base * power(base, exp-1);  // recursive: n^e = n × n^(e-1)
}

void printTable(int n, int upto) {                     // function define karo
    printf("Table of %d:\n", n);                       // output print karo
    for (int i = 1; i <= upto; i++)                    // integer variable
        printf("%d x %d = %d\n", n, i, n*i);   // print each row of table
}

void swap(int *a, int *b) {    // *a and *b are pointers (addresses)
    int temp = *a;             // *a dereferences the pointer (gets value)
    *a = *b;                   // assign b's value to a's location
    *b = temp;                 // assign original a's value to b's location
}

title: C Pointers
content:
#include <stdio.h>

int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }   // function for pointer-to-function demo

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    // ── Basic pointer ──────────────────────────────────────────
    int x = 42;            // regular variable
    int *ptr = &x;         // ptr is a POINTER — stores the ADDRESS of x (&x)

    printf("x        = %d\n",  x);          // 42 — value of x
    printf("address  = %p\n",  (void*)ptr); // memory address like 0x7fff...
    printf("*ptr     = %d\n",  *ptr);       // 42 — dereference: go to address, get value

    *ptr = 100;            // dereference to MODIFY x through the pointer
    printf("x after  = %d\n",  x);          // 100 — x was changed!

    // ── Pointer arithmetic ─────────────────────────────────────
    int arr[] = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};
    int *p = arr;          // p points to first element (arr = &arr[0])
    printf("Array via pointer: ");                     // output print karo
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)                        // integer variable
        printf("%d ", *(p + i));   // (p+i) = address of i-th element, * gets value
    printf("\n");                                      // output print karo

    // ── Pointer increment ─────────────────────────────────────
    printf("Stepping through: ");                      // output print karo
    p = arr;               // reset to start
    while (p <= &arr[4]) { // while p hasn't gone past last element
        printf("%d ", *p); // print value at current address
        p++;               // move pointer to NEXT integer (advances by 4 bytes)
    }
    printf("\n");                                      // output print karo

    // ── Double pointer (pointer to pointer) ───────────────────
    int **dptr = &ptr;         // dptr stores address of ptr
    printf("**dptr = %d\n", **dptr);  // 100 — double dereference

    // ── NULL pointer — pointer that points to nothing ─────────
    int *np = NULL;            // safest initial value for a pointer
    if (np == NULL) printf("Pointer is NULL (safe)\n"); // output print karo

    // ── Pointer to function ───────────────────────────────────
    int (*funcPtr)(int, int) = add;   // funcPtr points to the add function
    printf("Via funcPtr: %d\n", funcPtr(3, 4));  // 7 — call through pointer

    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>   // for malloc() and free()

// Node structure: each node has data and pointer to next node
struct Node {                                          // structure define karo
    int data;              // value stored in node
    struct Node *next;     // pointer to next node (NULL if last)
};

// Insert new node at beginning (prepend)
struct Node* insertFront(struct Node *head, int val) { // structure define karo
    struct Node *node = (struct Node*)malloc(sizeof(struct Node));   // allocate memory
    node->data = val;     // set value
    node->next = head;    // new node points to old head
    return node;          // new node becomes new head
}

// Insert new node at end (append)
struct Node* insertEnd(struct Node *head, int val) {   // structure define karo
    struct Node *node = (struct Node*)malloc(sizeof(struct Node)); // memory allocate karo
    node->data = val;                                  // pointer se member access karo
    node->next = NULL;    // new node is last, so next = NULL
    if (!head) return node;   // if list was empty, new node is the head
    struct Node *curr = head;                          // structure define karo
    while (curr->next) curr = curr->next;   // traverse to last node
    curr->next = node;   // attach new node after last
    return head;                                       // value return karo
}

// Delete node with given value
struct Node* deleteNode(struct Node *head, int val) {  // structure define karo
    if (!head) return NULL;   // empty list
    if (head->data == val) {  // if head itself is the node to delete
        struct Node *temp = head->next;                // structure define karo
        free(head);           // release memory
        return temp;          // new head is second node
    }
    struct Node *curr = head;                          // structure define karo
    while (curr->next && curr->next->data != val)  // find node before target
        curr = curr->next;                             // pointer se member access karo
    if (curr->next) {                    // found the target node
        struct Node *temp = curr->next;                // structure define karo
        curr->next = temp->next;         // skip over the target node
        free(temp);                      // release target's memory
    }
    return head;                                       // value return karo
}

// Print all nodes
void printList(struct Node *head) {                    // structure define karo
    while (head) {                                     // jab tak condition True ho
        printf("%d -> ", head->data);                  // output print karo
        head = head->next;    // move to next node
    }
    printf("NULL\n");        // NULL marks end of list
}

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    struct Node *head = NULL;              // empty list
    head = insertEnd(head, 10);            // 10
    head = insertEnd(head, 20);            // 10 -> 20
    head = insertEnd(head, 30);            // 10 -> 20 -> 30
    head = insertFront(head, 5);           // 5 -> 10 -> 20 -> 30
    printList(head);                       // 5 -> 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> NULL

    head = deleteNode(head, 20);           // remove 20
    printList(head);                       // 5 -> 10 -> 30 -> NULL

    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}

#include <stdio.h>

void decToBin(int n) {                                 // function define karo
    if (n > 1) decToBin(n / 2);                        // condition check karo
    printf("%d", n % 2);                               // output print karo
}

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    int n;
    printf("Enter decimal number: ");                  // output print karo
    scanf("%d", &n);                                   // input lo
    printf("Binary: "); decToBin(n); printf("\n");     // output print karo
    printf("Octal:  %o\n", n);                         // output print karo
    printf("Hex:    %X\n", n);                         // output print karo
    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int isPalindrome(char s[]) {                           // character variable
    int n = strlen(s);                                 // integer variable
    for (int i = 0; i < n/2; i++)                      // integer variable
        if (s[i] != s[n-1-i]) return 0;                // condition check karo
    return 1;                                          // value return karo
}

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    char words[][20] = {"racecar", "hello", "madam", "level", "world"}; // character variable
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)                        // integer variable
        printf("%s -> %s\n", words[i], isPalindrome(words[i]) ? "Palindrome" : "Not Palindrome"); // output print karo
    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}

#include <stdio.h>

int sumDigits(int n) {                                 // integer return karne wala function
    n = (n < 0) ? -n : n;
    int sum = 0;                                       // integer variable
    while (n > 0) { sum += n % 10; n /= 10; }          // jab tak condition True ho
    return sum;                                        // value return karo
}

int digitalRoot(int n) {                               // integer return karne wala function
    while (n >= 10) n = sumDigits(n);                  // jab tak condition True ho
    return n;                                          // value return karo
}

int main() {                                           // main function — yahan se shuru hota hai
    printf("Sum of digits of 12345 = %d\n", sumDigits(12345)); // 15
    printf("Sum of digits of 9999  = %d\n", sumDigits(9999));  // 36
    printf("Digital root of 9875  = %d\n", digitalRoot(9875)); // 2
    return 0;                                          // value return karo
}
